//: Realtime Database rules for the dashboard <-> server channel.
Deploy with:  firebase deploy --only database
or paste into Firebase console -> Realtime Database -> Rules.
The dashboard has no sign-in, so these rules allow unauthenticated access.
Anyone who knows this database URL can therefore read the command history
and queue a task. That is the accepted trade-off for a login-free dashboard.
The server uses the Admin SDK, which bypasses rules entirely — these only
constrain browsers.
Two things are still locked down, because they are correctness rather than
access control: /server/status is read-only (only the server publishes it),
and a command cannot be rewritten once the server has claimed it, which
would otherwise corrupt a run in progress.

server.//: Published by the server; browsers only read it.

//: One log stream per task UID, written by both snorkel_server and
snorkel_worker so a task's history reads as one sequence even though
two processes on two machines produced it. Browsers only read it.
The master switch, read by every server and worker.
Off means take no new work. Anything already running is left to
finish — a Claude session killed halfway is wasted, and a browser
abandoned mid-upload leaves a task in a state nobody asked for.
Scoped by workspace: one Firebase project can carry several independent
set-ups, and they must not share this. $workspace matches the
NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKSPACE / WORKSPACE setting of the dashboard, server and
worker that belong together. "default" is what a deployment that sets
nothing already is.
One entry per snorkel_worker, keyed by the machine it runs on.
Shared rather than nested under a machine, because a worker works for
machines it is not itself one of — there is no machine branch it
naturally belongs to. Browsers only read it.

The machines being worked, added from the dashboard.

settings.//: Written from the dashboard, read by the server.

logs.//: Written by the server only; the dashboard reads the tail.

ticker.//: One line, overwritten in place — the countdown to the next check.

worker.//: Published by snorkel_worker: how many tasks Claude has open.
